locations.name: Bridgeport Road
locations.blurb: The broad trade road south from Bridgeport, regularly patrolled by Crown troops. The twelve miles under the forest canopy are where trouble, such as it is, tends to find travelers.

locations.name: Hibble
locations.blurb: A tiny riverside hamlet of riverheart mustelins about five hundred feet north of the walls, treated by the town as an informal extension of Wexford.

locations.name: Bridgeport Gate
locations.blurb: The north gate and the town's main entrance, manned by chartreuse-clad Wardens. Its reinforced gates stand open from dawn to dusk.

locations.name: Wardenhall
locations.blurb: Barracks, offices, and training ground of the Wexford Wardens, a block west of Bridgeport Gate. Its doors are open from before dawn until well after dusk.

locations.name: Temple of the Lantern-Keeper
locations.blurb: A welcoming stone-and-timber temple of Mollo, whose beacon lantern burns each night above the treeline and offers shelter to travelers arriving after dark.

locations.name: Camber House
locations.blurb: A Crown-owned baronial guesthall for visiting nobles, inspectors, and envoys, with a Royal Adventuring Society agent in residence and a signal tower beside it.

locations.name: The Marble Canon
locations.blurb: The largest and most imposing building in Wexford, a pale marble temple of Absot near Springs Gate. Hierophant Halwen Marr presides.

locations.name: Springs Gate
locations.blurb: Wexford's second busiest entrance, opening west onto the forest road toward the hot springs and the coast.

locations.name: Hot Springs Road
locations.blurb: The road west from Springs Gate through the forest to the coast, with a branch to the hot springs. Safe by daylight.

locations.name: Westlink Road
locations.blurb: A bypass skirting the town's western edge, known as Warden's Cut, with a Warden toll station and stable where it meets Springs Road.

locations.name: Wexford Market
locations.blurb: A broad plaza market beside Spring Creek in the shadow of the tallest tower, famed for fine woodcraft.

locations.name: Waywarden Beacon
locations.blurb: Wexford's tallest structure, a civic signal tower rising from a courtyard enclosed by the halls of the timber, carpentry, and music guilds.

locations.name: The Limping Fiddler Inn
locations.blurb: Wexford's most accessible and adventurer-friendly inn, with a loud tavern, a stable yard, and its own smithy. Elowen Thistledown runs it.

locations.name: Adventurers' Guild Hall
locations.blurb: The regional hub for sanctioned adventurers, at the corner of the main north-south road and the east-west thoroughfare.

locations.name: The Gilded Alder Inn
locations.blurb: Wexford's most refined inn, with a dressed-stone ground floor, wood-fired kitchen, and a discreet carriage house at the end of a tree-lined lane.

locations.name: Greenbriar Timber Works
locations.blurb: A sprawling riverbank sawmill powered by a large waterwheel, one of Wexford's main economic engines.

locations.name: The Moot of Wexford
locations.blurb: The town's civic gathering hall, set apart from guild, noble, and temple authority, for feasts, public addresses, and disputes.

locations.name: Shrine of Olya Greenbriar
locations.blurb: The smallest of Wexford's temples and one of the most visible, a low garden-wrapped shrine on the corner of the fey crossing plaza.

locations.name: Feyward Spire
locations.blurb: The town's second-highest tower, rising from the civic administration building above a plaza inlaid with a replica of a fey crossing.

locations.name: Wexford Bridge
locations.blurb: The broad timber bridge over the Wex River that replaced the shallow ford the town was named for.

locations.name: The Laughing Bole Tavern
locations.blurb: A modest inn and public house beside Wexford Bridge, popular with millhands and with travelers from the Queen's Road.

locations.name: The Copper Hospice
locations.blurb: A hospice for the sick and wounded in the northern corner of east Wexford, open day and night. Matron Ilyra Fencrest runs it.

locations.name: Ironroot Lumber & Milling
locations.blurb: The town's second major timber concern, a rough, busy, waterwheel-driven mill on the east bank.

locations.name: The Eastgate
locations.blurb: The gate onto the deeper Wexwood, used mostly by work crews, Wardens, and expeditions. Sealed entirely after dusk.

locations.name: Riffel Road
locations.blurb: The longest and most perilous road through the Wexwood, running east to the Queen's Road near the Crown garrison at Riffel Station.

locations.name: Spring Creek Bridge
locations.blurb: A short, solid timber bridge over the creek ravine on the south side of town, narrow enough that wagons cross single file.

locations.name: Sands House
locations.blurb: The largest private residence in Wexford, the Crown's baronial house and the permanent home of Seneschal Maereth Ilthandor.

locations.name: Crown Barracks
locations.blurb: A fortified stone barracks across from Sands House, home of the Crown troops who patrol the roads. Captain Aurix Valemor commands.

locations.name: South Gate
locations.blurb: The least used of Wexford's four road gates, mostly for local traffic, with a person-sized door kept open in a gate leaf.

locations.name: River Road
locations.blurb: A quiet, isolated road south along the Wex toward the ruins of Nereth and Sand Manor, running uncomfortably close to the Dry Fells.
